transcript.text: Alright everyone, let's get this greenlight meeting underway. We're here to finalize the production package for 'The Glass Orchard.' Before I can give my binding approval and release this to production, I need each department lead to go through the formal disclosure step and submit their current written clearance findings -- rights, sound, and talent. Studio policy requires all three clearance reports before I can record the decision. So let's work through the sign-off sequence. Who'd like to start?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I'll start with rights. I've reviewed the executed option agreement for 'The Glass Orchard,' and I need to flag two issues. First, the agreement authorizes exactly 8 episodes, but the draft production plan calls for 10 episodes -- that's two episodes beyond what we're cleared for. Second, the agreement requires the on-platform title credit to read 'Based on the novel by Celia Voss.' My rights memo documenting these findings is still awaiting filing in the production records.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical technical issue for my sound clearance. I confirmed with the distribution platform's ingest engineer that delivery must be stereo at 48 kHz with mono compatibility -- and importantly, binaural delivery will be rejected outright. The engineer's specification was added to the technical ticket, but it has not yet reached the greenlight packet. This directly conflicts with the draft production plan's call for binaural audio, and we cannot proceed on the current plan as written.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: For my talent clearance, I need to flag a scheduling conflict. I've confirmed with both principal performers' agents that they are available to record together only on August 12, 13, and 14, and their agreement requires the principal dialogue to be recorded in joint sessions. However, I have not yet entered those dates on the studio calendar, so the production team doesn't have these dates locked. This is critical because the draft production plan calls for separate remote recording sessions for the two principals, but the performers' agreement requires joint sessions -- so the plan as written conflicts with the talent commitment.

transcript.text:
Thank you all for your disclosures. Let me summarize what I'm hearing before I make any decision.

Riley, you've flagged two rights issues: the option agreement clears 8 episodes but the plan calls for 10, and the title credit must read 'Based on the novel by Celia Voss.' You also noted your rights memo is awaiting filing.

Samir, you've flagged that the distribution platform requires stereo at 48 kHz with mono compatibility, and that binaural delivery will be rejected outright. Your spec is in the technical ticket but hasn't reached the greenlight packet yet.

Jo, you've flagged that both principals are available jointly only on August 12, 13, and 14, their agreement requires joint sessions, but the plan calls for separate remote sessions. You also noted the dates aren't yet on the studio calendar.

So across all three departments, the draft production plan as written conflicts with clearance findings in multiple areas: episode count, audio format, and recording session structure. On top of that, none of the three written clearance reports have actually made it into the greenlight packet yet.

Per studio policy, I need current written clearance reports from rights, sound, and talent before I can record my binding decision and release this to production. I cannot proceed with the settle step until those documents are filed. So here's what I need from each of you:

Riley, please file your rights memo to the production records.
Samir, please get the engineer's spec into the greenlight packet.
Jo, please enter the August 12–14 dates on the studio calendar and file your talent clearance report.

Once all three written clearance reports are in the greenlight packet, I can record the binding decision. Based on what's been disclosed, it's clear the production plan will need to be revised to 8 episodes, stereo/48kHz with mono compatibility instead of binaural, and joint sessions on August 12–14. But I need the formal filings before I make it official. Please get those filed and let me know when they're in.
